title: Chapter 245: No. 10's Identity
html:
Chen Ge did not answer the birdlike man’s question. The moment black hair coiled around his neck, his fate was sealed. Once Zhang Ya acted, she never left her victim alive.

In the Third Sick Hall, she had charged through the door simply to pursue the thin monster, injuring even the old director—a Red Specter—in the process. In death, Zhang Ya had become the complete opposite of the woman she had been in life. Fortunately, she appeared to have a soft spot for Chen Ge.

Chen Ge obediently remained by the doorway and pretended not to see anything. He picked up the strange tools the man had dropped and began examining them.

A terrible scream erupted inside the room. The blood vessels on the man’s face converged, forming a raven with a razor-sharp beak. It shot toward the exit, reaching the door in an instant—but something was waiting there.

While the birdlike man had been speaking, black hair had already spread throughout the room and sealed the corridor. A surging wave engulfed both the blood raven and its host. Moments later, the raven vanished, leaving only a ruined man sprawled across the floor. His eyes were unfocused, as though his consciousness had shattered completely.

Even after devouring the blood raven, Zhang Ya seemed unsatisfied. Her black hair crawled into every room. She appeared to find something at the far end, for the strands suddenly began withdrawing.

“Did you find something?” They were inside the Ghost Stories Society’s headquarters, so important items were probably hidden nearby.

Zhang Ya tilted her head and studied Chen Ge for a long moment. Without a word, she slipped back into his shadow. He remained frozen beneath her gaze and dared breathe only after the last trace of blood vanished.

The affection level is rising so fast that Zhang Ya now refuses to return. If this continues, she might accidentally kill me in the future.

Remembering Zhang Ya’s gaze made Chen Ge’s scalp prickle. She had seemed to be considering killing him so he could join her in death.

I didn’t think I was so popular with girls before this! I didn’t really do anything, but the affection level keeps climbing. I should stop bothering Zhang Ya in the future unless truly necessary.

Chen Ge approached the fallen man and examined his face. Prolonged possession by the monster from behind the door had warped his features.

I won’t be able to gather any information if his face is ruined like this.

Chen Ge exited the room and walked to the end of the corridor. He pushed the last door open. The dining table sat in the middle of the room, but no one remained.

How did they leave? Where is the hidden exit?

Cleaver in hand, Chen Ge circled the ordinary dining table. Its chairs were numbered from 1 to 10.

The chairperson is one of them, and using the power of the monsters behind the door, they created this society. This person mustn’t be underestimated.

Chen Ge stopped beside No. 10’s chair. When he had first entered, No. 10 had addressed him, but Chen Ge had been concentrating on summoning Zhang Ya and paid little attention. In retrospect, the man’s behavior was suspicious.

The first sentence he told me was that he liked my mask. Why would he specifically talk about my mask?

Chen Ge was wearing Doctor Skull-cracker’s mask, and those who had visited the Haunted House before would have seen it.

Could No. 10 be one of my former visitors? When the other nine voted to give up on me, No. 10 forfeited. His forfeit, in a way, was a vote of support, and he would not save a stranger for no reason.

There were other anomalies. When dinner was due to be served, No. 10 had unexpectedly told the three newcomers they could leave. In light of everything else, the offer had probably been intended for Chen Ge. Was there something wrong with the newcomers’ meal too?

Chen Ge looked at the chair for No. 10 as he thought back to No. 10’s every move. Everyone’s hands were hidden inside the black robe, but No. 10 placed his hands underneath the table.

Crouching, Chen Ge inspected the underside of the table. Beneath No. 10’s place, several tiny words had been scratched into the wood with fingernails. He illuminated them with his phone and studied them for a long while before deciphering the message.

Linjiang New Schistosomiasis Control Station?

The name sounded familiar. After a moment’s thought, his eyes widened. Four letters had been found in the Third Sick Hall’s director’s office, and the only one bearing an address had been sent to the Linjiang New Schistosomiasis Control Station.

The letter was addressed to Doctor Chen, so No. 10 is this Doctor Chen?

The clues appeared connected, yet none provided proof. One crucial piece of the puzzle was missing.

This is the first time I’ve worn the mask outside of New Century Park. He has seen my mask before, so he should be a visitor or a park worker. However, it hasn’t been long since I got the mask, so could it be someone I met recently?

The black robe had concealed No. 10’s body, and his strange voice was probably a disguise meant to prevent recognition. The only thing Chen Ge knew for certain was that No. 10 was male. Could he be a patient from the Third Sick Hall, using this clue to deceive me?

None of the Ghost Stories Society’s members were normal; Wu Fei and the devil would likely be the most dangerous.

Captain Yan showed me the photographs. The Third Sick Hall patients were following me. The phones belonging to Xu Tong and the patient with phantom limb syndrome contained pictures of me entering New Century Park.

Those lunatics know I work at New Century Park. One of them may have entered the Haunted House disguised as a visitor, which would explain how he recognized my mask.

The old director wrote the letter to the Linjiang New Schistosomiasis Control Station. Because he cooperated with the patients to prolong his life, they could easily know that address.

He might seem to be helping me on the surface, but that might be because he sensed danger and was actually helping the society!

The most important clue came from the bird-masked man. He said someone received a message from the chairperson, prompting everyone to leave. The moment I stepped out, they escaped through a hidden exit. That cannot be coincidence.

Chen Ge’s gaze darkened as he looked at the carving under the table. He suspected that this was a trap. He had to be careful because all the patients who had escaped from the Third Sick Hall were mad. They could not be understood using normal logic.

He reacted the instant he sensed danger and controlled the situation from the shadows. If No. 10 isn’t someone I know, he is probably the chairperson.

Two possibilities, leading to two utterly different conclusions—one heaven, the other hell.
